mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate level has a negative linear relationship with S&P 500 20-day forward returns: each 1 percentage point decrease in FEDFUNDS predicts a 0.4% increase in returns as lower rates reduce equity discount rates and boost cash flow valuation.
failure_condition: The linear regression slope of 20-day returns on FEDFUNDS is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% signals economic deterioration, triggering profit-taking and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings growth expectations decline.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) and stagnant monetary policy (FEDFUNDS < 2.0%) signal stagflation risk, causing equity sell-offs and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days as real rates rise without growth support.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 3.0 and FEDFUNDS < 2.0, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions (HOUST > 1400 and UNRATE < 3.0%), elevated housing starts signal economic overheating, prompting profit-taking and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days as growth expectations peak.
failure_condition: When HOUST > 1400 and UNRATE < 3.0%, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Negative industrial production growth (INDPRO growth rate < 0%) signals imminent recession, triggering equity sell-offs and negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days as manufacturing slowdowns erode corporate earnings.
failure_condition: When INDPRO growth rate is negative, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 > 2.0%) signals robust economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 days as corporate earnings growth expectations rise and risk appetite increases.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0%, 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong job growth (PAYEMS growth > 0.5%) combined with falling unemployment (UNRATE decline > 0.2%) signals labor market tightness, boosting consumer spending and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and UNRATE decline > 0.2%, 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) triggers near-term equity sell-offs as markets anticipate aggressive monetary tightening, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%, 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
